Attending: Sven Lindqvist, MD (General Surgery)
## Chief Complaint
RUQ abdominal pain and vomiting x 2 days
## HPI
47 y/o F experiencing homelessness (sleeps in her car, car recently towed, now at Example Shelter) presents with 2 days of RUQ pain after meals, nausea and vomiting. Fever 100.8F in ED. RUQ US: gallbladder wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, impacted stone in the neck. WBC 14.2. LFTs mildly elevated, bilirubin normal.

Acute calculous cholecystitis. IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone + metronidazole), NPO, laparoscopic cholecystectomy 09/07.
